title: The Parks crew leader whose good attitude is contagious
excerpt: Skip Brown greets residents with a smile and isn't too proud to empty a trash can. That's why he was formally commended.
body:
Most of us never think about the people who make a city event run smoothly. But someone noticed Skip Brown, and thought he deserved a thank-you.

Skip is a Parks Maintenance Crew Leader for the City of Rowlett. In a formal commendation sent to the director of the Parks Department, he was praised for something people kept seeing again and again: a professional who takes pride in how he does his job and how he treats people.

At Live on Main in downtown Rowlett on June 5, Skip greeted residents with a warm welcome that set the tone for the whole evening. Later that night, he spotted a full trash can and emptied it himself, without being asked and without a second thought. It's a small thing, but it's the kind of small thing that shows who someone is.

"Mr. Brown embodies the spirit of service that defines the best of Rowlett staff," the commendation reads. His positive attitude and leadership by example, it adds, "are not only commendable, but contagious."

The next time you're at a Rowlett park or a downtown event, look for the people in the city shirts keeping everything running. And if you see Skip, tell him thanks.
